summary: Checks whether a value is **not** convertible to a number.
description: `nonNumberLike(value)` is the same test as `!isNumberLike(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not convertible to a number; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonNumberLike(NaN); // => true
nonNumberLike(Infinity); // => true
nonNumberLike(""); // => true
nonNumberLike(null); // => true
nonNumberLike(1); // => false
nonNumberLike("1.5"); // => false
nonNumberLike(" 42 "); // => false
```
